title: Slow-cooker lentil and bacon soup
subtitle: Thick, smoky, and filling — a very easy all-day soup
excerpt: Green lentils and smoked lardons cooked all day with carrot, celery, and tomato into a deeply warming soup. Cheap, filling, and far better than a tin.
sourceNotes: Lentil and bacon soup is a staple of British home cooking. This version draws on French lentilles du Puy tradition of pairing lentils with smoked pork, adapted for the slow cooker.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Excellent batch-cook soup. Makes 6 large portions and keeps well in the fridge for 5 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Better the next day. The lentils soak up the broth and the smoky flavour deepens overnight.

content.text: Green lentils do not need soaking. They hold their shape better than red lentils, which makes this soup thicker and more substantial rather than completely smooth. If you prefer a velvety texture, use red lentils or blend half the finished soup.

Smoked lardons do the heavy lifting on flavour here. They release their fat into the soup during cooking and add a background of smoke that the lentils absorb over the long cook. Do not skip them or reduce the amount; they make the soup.
Serve with thick slices of bread. A splash of cider vinegar in the bowl adds sharpness if the soup tastes flat.

Add {{lentils-green}} of rinsed green lentils to the slow cooker. Add {{lardons}} of smoked lardons, {{onion}} diced onion, {{carrot}} of diced carrot, {{celery}} of sliced celery, and {{garlic}} of crushed garlic. Pour in {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes and {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock. Add {{thyme}} of thyme and {{bay-leaves}} of bay. Season with {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper-ground}} of pepper.

Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 7 to 8 hours. The lentils will be very soft and the broth thick. Discard the thyme and bay. Taste and adjust the seasoning. For a smoother texture, blend half the soup with a hand blender before serving.

rows.symptom: The lentils have dissolved into a mush
rows.cause: Green lentils cooked for 8 hours on LOW will become very soft and may lose their shape.
rows.fix: This is fine for a thick, smooth soup. If you prefer more texture next time, check at 6 hours and stop cooking when the lentils are tender but still whole.

rows.cause: Smoked lardons are high in salt, and the stock also contributes salt.
rows.fix: Add a diced raw potato and cook on HIGH for 20 minutes; it will absorb some of the salt. Add a splash of water to dilute.

rows.cause: More liquid was added than the lentils could absorb.
rows.fix: Cook on HIGH with the lid off for 30 minutes to reduce. Alternatively, blend more of the soup to add body.

rows.cause: The lardons lacked smokiness, or the stock was mild.
rows.fix: Add a teaspoon of smoked paprika and stir well. A squeeze of lemon juice will also lift the soup.

content.text: Lentil and bacon soup has roots in French country cooking, where green lentils and smoked pork are a classic combination. In Britain it is a practical winter soup made from cheap, long-shelf-life ingredients. It is one of the best arguments for keeping a bag of green lentils in the cupboard at all times.
